#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Input shapes the dev inbox does not contain.

The dev set has 24 emails and the held-out inbox has ~40 "from the same company,
the same kinds of surprises, none of the same strings".  The cheapest way to find
real defects is not to re-read those 24 — it is to ask what shape of input they
happen not to include, and build it.

Every case here is something a real RFQ inbox produces weekly.  Run it and read
the findings; it reports rather than merely passes, because some of these have no
single right answer and the interesting part is what the system actually does.

    python tests/test_shapes.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from email.message import EmailMessage
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from rfq.cli import _load_dotenv  # noqa: E402
from rfq.pipeline import run  # noqa: E402

CSV_BOM = (
    b'Qty,UOM,Size,Description\n'
    b'12,EA,"1-1/2""","90 elbow, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
    b'6,EA,"1-1/2""","Tee, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
    b'8,EA,"1-1/2""","Union, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
)


def msg(frm, subject, body, *, date, mid, attachments=(), in_reply_to=None, headers=(), charset=None):
    m = EmailMessage()
    m["From"] = frm
    m["To"] = "rfq@ridgeline-supply.example"
    m["Subject"] = subject
    m["Date"] = date
    m["Message-ID"] = mid
    if in_reply_to:
        m["In-Reply-To"] = in_reply_to
        m["References"] = in_reply_to
    for k, v in headers:
        m[k] = v
    if charset:
        m.set_content(body, charset=charset)
    else:
        m.set_content(body)
    for name, mime, data in attachments:
        maintype, _, subtype = mime.partition("/")
        m.add_attachment(data, maintype=maintype, subtype=subtype, filename=name)
    return m


def build(inbox: Path) -> None:
    # S001 — our rep forwards a customer email; the BOM is attached to the INNER message
    inner = msg(
        "Priya Raman <priya@hollismech.example>",
        "material list - condensate return",
        "Marcus,\n\nList attached for job HM-7716. Please price it.\n\nPriya",
        date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0600",
        mid="<inner-1@hollismech.example>",
        attachments=[("HM-7716_list.csv", "text/csv", CSV_BOM)],
    )
    outer = msg(
        "Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@ridgeline-supply.example>",
        "FW: material list - condensate return",
        "RFQ desk - please quote this for Priya, she needs it Friday.\n\nMarcus",
        date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
        mid="<s001@ridgeline-supply.example>",
        attachments=[("forwarded.eml", "message/rfc822", inner.as_bytes())],
    )
    (inbox / "S001.eml").write_bytes(outer.as_bytes())

    # S002 — two attachments with the SAME filename and different contents
    second = CSV_BOM.replace(b"12,EA", b"40,EA").replace(b"90 elbow", b"45 elbow")
    (inbox / "S002.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Dale Thibodeaux <dale@pelicanbay.example>",
            "two areas - please quote both sheets",
            "Both sheets attached, area A and area B. Price them separately.",
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s002@pelicanbay.example>",
            attachments=[("sheet.csv", "text/csv", CSV_BOM), ("sheet.csv", "text/csv", second)],
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S003 — windows-1252 body (an em dash and a degree sign), as Outlook sends
    body = "Hi,\n\nPlease quote — urgent:\n\n6 ea – 2\" 90° elbow, SW 3000# A105\n4 ea – 2\" tee, SW 3000# A105\n\nRegards,\nJosé"
    (inbox / "S003.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Jose Alvarez <jose@gulfmech.example>",
            "urgent - 2in socket weld fittings",
            body,
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s003@gulfmech.example>",
            charset="windows-1252",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S004 — out-of-office.  The brief names it; dev only has a bounce.
    (inbox / "S004.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Gwen Aldridge <galdridge@ironwoodskids.example>",
            "Automatic reply: RFQ - Skid 14 piping package",
            "I am out of the office until 10 November with limited access to email.\n"
            "For urgent purchasing matters contact Dana Reyes.\n\nGwen",
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 12:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s004@ironwoodskids.example>",
            headers=[("Auto-Submitted", "auto-replied"), ("X-Auto-Response-Suppress", "All")],
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S005/S006/S007 — a three-step thread: request, revision, revision again
    rfq = msg(
        "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
        "Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
        "Hi,\n\nPlease quote:\n\n1) 20 jts - 2\" SCH 40 A53B ERW pipe, T&C\n"
        "2) 10 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron 90 ell, black\n"
        "3) 6 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron tee, black\n\nTomas",
        date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:00:00 -0600",
        mid="<s005@southfork.example>",
    )
    (inbox / "S005.eml").write_bytes(rfq.as_bytes())
    (inbox / "S006.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
            "Re: Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
            "Change line 1 to 26 jts. Everything else stays.\n\nTomas",
            date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s006@southfork.example>",
            in_reply_to="<s005@southfork.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )
    (inbox / "S007.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
            "Re: Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
            "Sorry - also drop line 3, and add 4 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron union, black.\n\nTomas",
            date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s007@southfork.example>",
            in_reply_to="<s006@southfork.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S008/S009 — same sender, same generic subject, DIFFERENT orders.
    # These must NOT be collapsed into a duplicate.
    (inbox / "S008.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Cody Landry <cody@landryoil.example>",
            "pricing request",
            "Need pricing:\n\n10 ea - 3\" 150# RF weld neck flange, A105\n",
            date="Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s008@landryoil.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )
    (inbox / "S009.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Cody Landry <cody@landryoil.example>",
            "pricing request",
            "Need pricing:\n\n25 ea - 6\" 300# RF blind flange, A105\n",
            date="Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s009@landryoil.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S010 — units and numbers the dev set never exercises
    (inbox / "S010.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Ben Szymanski <ben@oakhollow.example>",
            "consumables for the glycol line",
            "Hi,\n\nPlease quote:\n\n"
            "twelve lengths of 1\" SCH 40 galvanized pipe, TBE\n"
            "1,200 ft of 3/4\" SCH 40 galvanized pipe, TBE\n"
            "3 gal - thread sealant\n"
            "2 bags - pipe joint compound\n"
            "1 case - shop rags\n"
            "4 pair - welding gloves\n"
            "2 dozen - 1/2\" hex nuts, zinc\n"
            "2.5 ft of 2\" pipe insulation\n\nBen",
            date="Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s010@oakhollow.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )


EXPECT = {
    "S001": "forwarded email: the BOM is attached to the INNER message (3 items)",
    "S002": "two attachments share one filename; both sheets must survive (6 items)",
    "S003": "windows-1252 body with em dash / accents (2 items)",
    "S004": "out-of-office -> auto_reply, no items",
    "S005": "original request (3 items)",
    "S006": "revision 1 -> complete order, line 1 becomes 26 (3 items)",
    "S007": "revision 2 -> builds on revision 1: drop line 3, add a union (3 items)",
    "S008": "same subject as S009 but a DIFFERENT order (1 item)",
    "S009": "must NOT be marked a duplicate of S008 (1 item)",
    "S010": "units GAL/BAG/CS/PR/DZ, 'twelve', '1,200', '2.5'",
}


def main() -> int:
    _load_dotenv()
    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rfq-shapes-"))
    try:
        inbox = tmp / "emails"
        inbox.mkdir()
        build(inbox)

        parsed, cost, results = run(
            inbox, cache_dir=REPO / "cache", api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"), concurrency=4
        )
        by_id = {r.id: r for r in results}

        for eid in sorted(parsed):
            row, res = parsed[eid], by_id[eid]
            print(f"\n{eid}  — {EXPECT[eid]}")
            docs = ", ".join(f"{d.source}:{d.kind}" for d in res.documents)
            print(f"   class={row['classification']}  review={row['needs_review']}"
                  f"  dup={row['duplicate_of']}  revises={row['revises']}  lines={len(row['line_items'])}")
            print(f"   docs: {docs}")
            if row["needs_review"]:
                print(f"   reason: {(row['review_reason'] or '')[:150]}")
            for l in row["line_items"]:
                print(f"     qty={str(l['qty']):<6} {str(l['uom']):<5} {l['description'][:66]}")

        print(f"\n{len(parsed)} emails, {cost['model_calls']} calls, ${cost['cold_run']['cost_usd']:.4f}")
        return 0
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

MAX_NESTING = 3


def documentize_all(attachment, page_cap: int = DEFAULT_PAGE_CAP, _depth: int = 0) -> list[Document]:
    """One attachment -> one or more Documents, following forwarded messages inward.

    An attached email is a container, not a leaf.  Its own attachments become
    documents in their own right, under their own filenames, so a line extracted
    from a forwarded spreadsheet reports the spreadsheet as its source rather than
    the envelope it travelled in.  Depth-limited: a chain of forwards is ordinary,
    a thousand nested messages is a denial-of-service.
    """
    doc = documentize(attachment, page_cap)
    inner = doc.meta.pop("_inner_attachments", None)
    out = [doc]
    if inner and _depth < MAX_NESTING:
        for att in inner:
            out.extend(documentize_all(att, page_cap, _depth + 1))
    return out

content.text:
## What I tested, and what it found

I built the whole list as `tests/test_shapes.py` and ran it. **8 of 10 were already right; 2 were not.**

| shape | result |
|---|---|
| Rep forwards a customer email, **BOM attached to the inner message** | ❌ → **fixed** |
| Two attachments sharing one filename, different contents | ✅ both survive, 6 lines |
| windows-1252 body (em dash, `°`, `José`) | ✅ |
| Out-of-office auto-reply | ✅ `auto_reply`, 0 lines |
| 3-step revision chain (RFQ → rev → rev) | ⚠️ right answer, **false review flag** → fixed |
| Two different orders, same generic subject, same sender | ✅ **not** collapsed into a duplicate |
| Units `GAL BAG CS PR DZ`, "twelve", "1,200", "2.5" | ✅ all 8 correct |

### Finding 1 — forwarded email, attachment one level deeper

This is **E016's exact shape with the CSV one level in**. We read the attached message as a leaf, saw only its covering note, and lost all three items. Flagged, so not a silent loss — but lost.

Underneath it was a second bug I'd never have guessed: the payload arrived as **base64 text**. RFC 2046 says `message/rfc822` must be 7-bit, so Python won't record a base64 CTE and won't decode one — but gateways base64 attached messages anyway. A parse yielding neither `From` nor `Subject` is the tell; we now decode and retry.

```
before:  docs: body, forwarded.eml                      → 0 lines
after:   docs: body, forwarded.eml, HM-7716_list.csv    → 3 lines
```

### Finding 2 — revision chain

`"change line 1"` names a request the message doesn't contain — genuinely unresolvable, right up until we find that request in the inbox and merge against it. Once `revises` is set, it's resolved. Was costing `needs_review` precision.

---

## What I'd still test, ranked

**Worth doing (likely on held-out):**

1. **PO that selects by description, not number** — *"go ahead with the flanges and the pipe"*. I named this in `DECISIONS.md` as an expected failure; I've never actually run it.
2. **Quoted-history detection against more client formats** — Apple Mail, Outlook Web, Gmail mobile, a French/German `Von:`/`De:` header block. Our splitter is the single biggest hallucination guard and it's tuned on four formats.
3. **A scan with no item-number column** — our strip de-duplication anchors on that index; without one, overlapping strips could double-count.
4. **Table where qty is to the *right* of the description**, or a two-column-pairs layout.

**Lower value:**

5. Cache file corrupted mid-write (handled by try/except, untested).
6. 300-page PDF end-to-end (the cap is tested at the unit level, not the run level).
7. Inline `cid:` reference pointing at a part that isn't there.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Input shapes the dev inbox does not contain.

The dev set has 24 emails and the held-out inbox has ~40 "from the same company,
the same kinds of surprises, none of the same strings".  The cheapest way to find
real defects is not to re-read those 24 — it is to ask what shape of input they
happen not to include, and build it.

Every case here is something a real RFQ inbox produces weekly.  Run it and read
the findings; it reports rather than merely passes, because some of these have no
single right answer and the interesting part is what the system actually does.

    python tests/test_shapes.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from email.message import EmailMessage
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from rfq.cli import _load_dotenv  # noqa: E402
from rfq.pipeline import run  # noqa: E402

CSV_BOM = (
    b'Qty,UOM,Size,Description\n'
    b'12,EA,"1-1/2""","90 elbow, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
    b'6,EA,"1-1/2""","Tee, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
    b'8,EA,"1-1/2""","Union, SW, 3000#, A105"\n'
)


def msg(frm, subject, body, *, date, mid, attachments=(), in_reply_to=None, headers=(), charset=None):
    m = EmailMessage()
    m["From"] = frm
    m["To"] = "rfq@ridgeline-supply.example"
    m["Subject"] = subject
    m["Date"] = date
    m["Message-ID"] = mid
    if in_reply_to:
        m["In-Reply-To"] = in_reply_to
        m["References"] = in_reply_to
    for k, v in headers:
        m[k] = v
    if charset:
        m.set_content(body, charset=charset)
    else:
        m.set_content(body)
    for name, mime, data in attachments:
        maintype, _, subtype = mime.partition("/")
        m.add_attachment(data, maintype=maintype, subtype=subtype, filename=name)
    return m


def build(inbox: Path) -> None:
    # S001 — our rep forwards a customer email; the BOM is attached to the INNER message
    inner = msg(
        "Priya Raman <priya@hollismech.example>",
        "material list - condensate return",
        "Marcus,\n\nList attached for job HM-7716. Please price it.\n\nPriya",
        date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0600",
        mid="<inner-1@hollismech.example>",
        attachments=[("HM-7716_list.csv", "text/csv", CSV_BOM)],
    )
    outer = msg(
        "Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@ridgeline-supply.example>",
        "FW: material list - condensate return",
        "RFQ desk - please quote this for Priya, she needs it Friday.\n\nMarcus",
        date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
        mid="<s001@ridgeline-supply.example>",
        attachments=[("forwarded.eml", "message/rfc822", inner.as_bytes())],
    )
    (inbox / "S001.eml").write_bytes(outer.as_bytes())

    # S002 — two attachments with the SAME filename and different contents
    second = CSV_BOM.replace(b"12,EA", b"40,EA").replace(b"90 elbow", b"45 elbow")
    (inbox / "S002.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Dale Thibodeaux <dale@pelicanbay.example>",
            "two areas - please quote both sheets",
            "Both sheets attached, area A and area B. Price them separately.",
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s002@pelicanbay.example>",
            attachments=[("sheet.csv", "text/csv", CSV_BOM), ("sheet.csv", "text/csv", second)],
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S003 — windows-1252 body (an em dash and a degree sign), as Outlook sends
    body = "Hi,\n\nPlease quote — urgent:\n\n6 ea – 2\" 90° elbow, SW 3000# A105\n4 ea – 2\" tee, SW 3000# A105\n\nRegards,\nJosé"
    (inbox / "S003.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Jose Alvarez <jose@gulfmech.example>",
            "urgent - 2in socket weld fittings",
            body,
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s003@gulfmech.example>",
            charset="windows-1252",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S004 — out-of-office.  The brief names it; dev only has a bounce.
    (inbox / "S004.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Gwen Aldridge <galdridge@ironwoodskids.example>",
            "Automatic reply: RFQ - Skid 14 piping package",
            "I am out of the office until 10 November with limited access to email.\n"
            "For urgent purchasing matters contact Dana Reyes.\n\nGwen",
            date="Mon, 02 Nov 2026 12:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s004@ironwoodskids.example>",
            headers=[("Auto-Submitted", "auto-replied"), ("X-Auto-Response-Suppress", "All")],
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S005/S006/S007 — a three-step thread: request, revision, revision again
    rfq = msg(
        "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
        "Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
        "Hi,\n\nPlease quote:\n\n1) 20 jts - 2\" SCH 40 A53B ERW pipe, T&C\n"
        "2) 10 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron 90 ell, black\n"
        "3) 6 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron tee, black\n\nTomas",
        date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:00:00 -0600",
        mid="<s005@southfork.example>",
    )
    (inbox / "S005.eml").write_bytes(rfq.as_bytes())
    (inbox / "S006.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
            "Re: Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
            "Change line 1 to 26 jts. Everything else stays.\n\nTomas",
            date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s006@southfork.example>",
            in_reply_to="<s005@southfork.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )
    (inbox / "S007.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Tomas Reyes <treyes@southfork.example>",
            "Re: Tank farm phase 3 - pricing",
            "Sorry - also drop line 3, and add 4 ea - 2\" 150# malleable iron union, black.\n\nTomas",
            date="Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s007@southfork.example>",
            in_reply_to="<s006@southfork.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S008/S009 — same sender, same generic subject, DIFFERENT orders.
    # These must NOT be collapsed into a duplicate.
    (inbox / "S008.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Cody Landry <cody@landryoil.example>",
            "pricing request",
            "Need pricing:\n\n10 ea - 3\" 150# RF weld neck flange, A105\n",
            date="Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s008@landryoil.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )
    (inbox / "S009.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Cody Landry <cody@landryoil.example>",
            "pricing request",
            "Need pricing:\n\n25 ea - 6\" 300# RF blind flange, A105\n",
            date="Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s009@landryoil.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )

    # S010 — units and numbers the dev set never exercises
    (inbox / "S010.eml").write_bytes(
        msg(
            "Ben Szymanski <ben@oakhollow.example>",
            "consumables for the glycol line",
            "Hi,\n\nPlease quote:\n\n"
            "twelve lengths of 1\" SCH 40 galvanized pipe, TBE\n"
            "1,200 ft of 3/4\" SCH 40 galvanized pipe, TBE\n"
            "3 gal - thread sealant\n"
            "2 bags - pipe joint compound\n"
            "1 case - shop rags\n"
            "4 pair - welding gloves\n"
            "2 dozen - 1/2\" hex nuts, zinc\n"
            "2.5 ft of 2\" pipe insulation\n\nBen",
            date="Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0600",
            mid="<s010@oakhollow.example>",
        ).as_bytes()
    )


EXPECT = {
    "S001": "forwarded email: the BOM is attached to the INNER message (3 items)",
    "S002": "two attachments share one filename; both sheets must survive (6 items)",
    "S003": "windows-1252 body with em dash / accents (2 items)",
    "S004": "out-of-office -> auto_reply, no items",
    "S005": "original request (3 items)",
    "S006": "revision 1 -> complete order, line 1 becomes 26 (3 items)",
    "S007": "revision 2 -> builds on revision 1: drop line 3, add a union (3 items)",
    "S008": "same subject as S009 but a DIFFERENT order (1 item)",
    "S009": "must NOT be marked a duplicate of S008 (1 item)",
    "S010": "units GAL/BAG/CS/PR/DZ, 'twelve', '1,200', '2.5'",
}


def main() -> int:
    _load_dotenv()
    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rfq-shapes-"))
    try:
        inbox = tmp / "emails"
        inbox.mkdir()
        build(inbox)

        parsed, cost, results = run(
            inbox, cache_dir=REPO / "cache", api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"), concurrency=4
        )
        by_id = {r.id: r for r in results}

        for eid in sorted(parsed):
            row, res = parsed[eid], by_id[eid]
            print(f"\n{eid}  — {EXPECT[eid]}")
            docs = ", ".join(f"{d.source}:{d.kind}" for d in res.documents)
            print(f"   class={row['classification']}  review={row['needs_review']}"
                  f"  dup={row['duplicate_of']}  revises={row['revises']}  lines={len(row['line_items'])}")
            print(f"   docs: {docs}")
            if row["needs_review"]:
                print(f"   reason: {(row['review_reason'] or '')[:150]}")
            for l in row["line_items"]:
                print(f"     qty={str(l['qty']):<6} {str(l['uom']):<5} {l['description'][:66]}")

        print(f"\n{len(parsed)} emails, {cost['model_calls']} calls, ${cost['cold_run']['cost_usd']:.4f}")
        return 0
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Running it

## One setup step

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .
```

Windows: `py -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\pip install -e .`

Python 3.11+. Dependencies: `openai`, `openpyxl`, `python-docx`, `pymupdf`, `pillow` — all pure
wheels, no system packages, no poppler, no tesseract. Nothing is Linux-specific, so there is no
Dockerfile to need.

## The command

```bash
rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
```

or, without installing:

```bash
python parse.py parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
```

`--out parsed.json` also writes `parsed.cost.json` beside it. Add `--traces traces/` for a
per-email record of what was found, what each document was judged to be, and every line that
was dropped and why.

Exit codes: `0` the run completed; `2` it completed but some emails could not reach a model
(those come back flagged); `1` it could not start.

## The API key

Read from `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or from a `.env` file beside this README containing
`OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...`. 

**With no key at all the dev inbox still runs**, replayed from the recorded answers in
`cache/`, and produces byte-identical output. That is the property the brief asks for, and it
is tested below.

## Models

| stage | default | why |
|---|---|---|
| classify | `gpt-4.1-mini` | short input, one cheap call, gates everything downstream |
| extract (text) | `gpt-4.1` | the context-carrying judgement lives here |
| extract (pictures) | `gpt-4.1` | photos, scans, pasted screenshots |

Override per run with `--model-classify / --model-extract / --model-vision`, or the env vars
`RFQ_MODEL_CLASSIFY / RFQ_MODEL_EXTRACT / RFQ_MODEL_VISION`.

These are the models the committed cache was recorded with, so a keyless replay only works on
the defaults. If your key cannot reach one of them, `rfq/llm.py` falls through to the nearest
equivalent (`gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`) rather than failing the email, and records the answer
under the model that was *asked for* so later replays still hit.

The account this was built with also reached `gpt-5.x`. I did not default to it: it is not
universally available on other keys, I cannot report its price accurately, and on the one
measurement that mattered it was not better — see `DECISIONS.md`.

## What a run costs

Dev inbox, 24 emails, from an empty cache:

```
58 model calls · 96,424 prompt tokens · 19,891 completion tokens · $0.2882
$0.0120 per email
```

Spread is wide and deliberate. The four emails that carry no items — a vendor quote, a status
inquiry, a bounce, a newsletter — cost **$0.0007 each**, because classification runs first and
stops there. The expensive ones are the big documents: `$0.0380` for the 32-line two-page phone
scan, `$0.0332` for the 44-line PDF, `$0.0317` for the 50-line two-tab workbook.

A second run on the same inbox costs **$0.0000** and makes **0** model calls.

`parsed.cost.json` always reports both what this run spent and what the inbox would cost cold,
so a replay still tells you the real number. Prices come from the table in `rfq/llm.py` and are
printed with the report; override with `RFQ_PRICE_<MODEL>_IN` / `_OUT` if they drift.

## Verifying the four properties

```bash
# 1 + 2 — replayable with no key, and free the second time
rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out a.json      # cold: 58 calls, $0.2882
rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out b.json      # 0 calls, $0.0000
mv .env .env.off && rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out c.json && mv .env.off .env
shasum -a 256 a.json b.json c.json                   # all three identical

# 3 — one bad email never takes down the run
python tests/test_resilience.py

# 4 — cost
cat parsed.cost.json
```

## Scoring it yourself

```bash
python scripts/score.py parsed.json data/dev/answer_key.json
python scripts/score.py parsed.json data/dev/answer_key.json --detail E009
python data/check_format.py parsed.json --emails data/dev/emails
```

`scripts/score.py` implements the brief's metrics in the order it says it grades them, with the
spelling-equivalence table the README describes. Current dev numbers are in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Screen recording

<!-- TODO: paste the link here before sending. -->

## Layout

```
rfq/ingest.py      MIME, body text, current-vs-quoted split, header signals, fingerprints
rfq/documents.py   attachments -> uniform Documents; routing by magic bytes
rfq/classify.py    the seven classes, the code vetoes, the cost gate
rfq/extract.py     per-document extraction, page strips, revision merge
rfq/verify.py      groundedness, uom vocabulary, qty sanity, de-duplication
rfq/link.py        duplicates, revisions, the needs_review rules
rfq/llm.py         the single model call site: cache, cost ledger, retries, fallbacks
rfq/prompts.py     what the model is told
rfq/pipeline.py    phase A (parallel, per email) and phase B (ordered, per inbox)
cache/             recorded model answers — committed, this is what makes replay work
scripts/score.py   the grader, as described in data/README.md
tests/             the resilience inbox
```

## Results

**One real bug found, two predictions resolved.**

### Test 2 — quoted-history split (the one that mattered)

13 client formats, free, no model:

```
gmail desktop · gmail mobile · apple mail · outlook desktop ·
outlook web · outlook bare header · gmail forward · apple forward ·
bare > quoting · lotus notes                              ✅ all pass

german outlook   ❌  FAIL — old order leaked into the current message
french outlook   ❌  FAIL
spanish outlook  ❌  FAIL
```

Plus 4 negative cases (an ordinary request that merely *looks* header-ish — `"the list from the yard"`, `"On the skid we need:"`, a ship-to block with `To:`) — all correctly left whole.

The three failures matter because they fail **silently**. An unrecognised `Von:`/`Gesendet:` block doesn't error — it hands last month's order to the extractor as if it were today's request, which is grading failure #2. Spanish is genuinely plausible on the Gulf Coast. Header words are now localised across six languages; a match still needs the From-like line *plus* two follow-up fields within four lines, so the negatives still pass.

### Test 1 — PO selecting by description

```
"Go ahead with the flanges and the pipe. Hold the valves and the gaskets."

→ purchase_order, 2 lines:
    8 EA    3" 150# RF weld neck flange, A105, STD bore
    120 FT  3" SCH 40 A53B ERW pipe, PE
```

Valve and gasket correctly held back. **I had predicted this would fail** in `DECISIONS.md`. It doesn't. I corrected the prediction in place rather than deleting it — an untested prediction and a tested one aren't the same kind of claim, and most of that section is still the first kind.

### Test 3 — scan with no item-number column

24 rows, read as overlapping strips with no index to anchor de-duplication on → **24 lines, no repeats**, and the `ALL FITTINGS THREADED 3000# A105 UNLESS NOTED` default carried onto every row. The `_leading_numbers_are_an_index` guard correctly declined to dedupe.

---

## Where the repo stands

```
tests/test_quoted_split.py   13 clients + 4 negatives   free, no key
tests/test_resilience.py      8 broken emails            ~$0.00 cached
tests/test_shapes.py         12 unusual shapes           ~$0.09 cold

dev: 0 silent losses · 0 hallucinated · classification 24/24
     lines P/R 100% · qty 99.1% · context 100% · links 100%
```

11 commits. Five real bugs found since the dev set saturated, none of them visible on dev:

1. empty email + corrupt attachment → unflaggable silent loss
2. PDF with text *and* images → pixels never read
3. spreadsheet > ~2,000 rows → a third dropped, no flag
4. forwarded email with the order one level deeper → items lost
5. non-English quoted-history block → old order leaked in

That's the honest answer to your earlier question about working without an answer key: every one of those came from asking *"what shape does dev not contain?"* and building it — not from re-reading the 24.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The deterministic layer: how bytes become documents.  No model, no key, free.

Everything here was a defect at some point, so everything here is a regression
test. The two at the top were found by building an input shape the dev inbox does
not contain, verified by hand, and then had no test guarding them — which is a fix
waiting to come undone.

The dev-routing block at the end exists for a different reason: it pins the exact
text the committed cache was recorded against. Change how a PDF or a sheet is
rendered and every recorded answer silently stops matching, the keyless replay
breaks, and the run looks fine while calling the model for all 24 emails.

    python tests/test_documents.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from rfq.documents import (  # noqa: E402
    MAX_DOC_ROWS,
    cap_rows,
    documentize,
    documentize_all,
    read_pdf,
    read_xlsx,
    sniff,
)
from rfq.extract import CHUNK_ROWS, _chunks  # noqa: E402
from rfq.ingest import ingest  # noqa: E402

DEV = REPO / "data" / "dev" / "emails"
checks: list[tuple[bool, str]] = []


def check(ok: bool, label: str, detail: str = "") -> None:
    checks.append((bool(ok), f"{label}{('  — ' + detail) if detail else ''}"))


def _sheet(n_rows: int) -> bytes:
    from openpyxl import Workbook

    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "FITTINGS - SW 3000#"
    ws.append(["Unit 9 - full BOM"])
    ws.append(["ALL FITTINGS SW 3000# A105 UNLESS NOTED"])
    ws.append(["ITEM", "QTY", "UOM", "SIZE", "DESCRIPTION"])
    for i in range(1, n_rows + 1):
        ws.append([i, (i % 40) + 1, "EA", '1-1/2"', "90 Elbow"])
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def _hybrid_pdf() -> bytes:
    """A typed covering note with a screenshot of a BOM pasted into it."""
    import pymupdf

    shot = ingest(DEV / "E010.eml").attachments[0].data  # a real spreadsheet screenshot
    doc = pymupdf.open()
    page = doc.new_page()
    page.insert_text((60, 70), "Ridgeline RFQ - Job 4412 shutdown materials", fontsize=13)
    page.insert_text((60, 95), "Please quote the items on the sheet below.", fontsize=10)
    page.insert_image(pymupdf.Rect(60, 120, 520, 460), stream=shot)
    page.insert_text((60, 500), "Delivery to Plant 2 dock. Terms net 30.", fontsize=10)
    return doc.tobytes()


class _Att:
    def __init__(self, filename, mime, data):
        self.filename, self.mime, self.data = filename, mime, data
        self.inline, self.content_id, self.size = False, None, len(data)


def main() -> int:
    # ---- a PDF carrying BOTH text and pictures -------------------------------- #
    # Was: any text layer meant "text document" and the pixels were never read, so a
    # screenshot of the order was invisible.  Silent, because the covering note parses.
    d = read_pdf(_hybrid_pdf(), "hybrid.pdf")
    check(d.kind == "mixed", "hybrid PDF is routed as mixed", f"got {d.kind!r}")
    check(len(d.images) >= 1, "its embedded picture is extracted", f"{len(d.images)} image(s)")
    check("Job 4412" in d.text, "its typed text is still read")

    # a logo-sized raster must NOT drag a page into mixed
    import pymupdf

    small = pymupdf.open()
    p = small.new_page()
    p.insert_text((60, 70), "Please quote the list below: 10 ea 2in gate valve, 800#", fontsize=11)
    p.insert_image(pymupdf.Rect(40, 700, 110, 740), stream=ingest(DEV / "E017.eml").attachments[0].data)
    d2 = read_pdf(small.tobytes(), "letterhead.pdf")
    check(d2.kind == "text", "a letterhead logo does not make a page mixed", f"got {d2.kind!r}")

    # ---- a spreadsheet past the row cap --------------------------------------- #
    # Was: truncated at 60k characters inside the extractor with truncated=False,
    # so a third of the order vanished and the email looked like a clean parse.
    big = documentize(_Att("Unit9.xlsx", "application/vnd.ms-excel", _sheet(3000)))
    check(big.truncated, "an oversized sheet is marked truncated")
    check(
        big.meta.get("rows_total", 0) > big.meta.get("rows_read", 0) == MAX_DOC_ROWS,
        "it reports how much it did not read",
        f"{big.meta.get('rows_read')} of {big.meta.get('rows_total')}",
    )
    check(len(big.text.splitlines()) == MAX_DOC_ROWS, "and is actually cut to the cap")

    small_sheet = documentize(_Att("small.xlsx", "application/vnd.ms-excel", _sheet(50)))
    check(not small_sheet.truncated, "an ordinary sheet is not truncated")

    # chunking must be bounded by ROWS: the constraint is the model's output length
    chunks = _chunks(big.text)
    check(
        all(len(c.splitlines()) <= CHUNK_ROWS for c in chunks),
        "no chunk exceeds the row budget",
        f"{len(chunks)} chunks, max {max(len(c.splitlines()) for c in chunks)} rows",
    )

    # ---- a forwarded message is a container, not a leaf ----------------------- #
    bounce = ingest(DEV / "E013.eml")
    docs = documentize_all(bounce.attachments[0])
    check(len(docs) >= 1 and docs[0].meta.get("attached_message"), "an attached .eml is parsed")
    check(
        "_inner_attachments" not in docs[0].meta,
        "its inner-attachment handle is consumed, not leaked into traces",
    )

    # ---- routing by content, never by filename -------------------------------- #
    check(sniff(b"%PDF-1.4\n...", "application/octet-stream", "x.txt") == "pdf", "magic bytes beat the mime type")
    check(sniff(b"Qty,UOM\n1,EA\n", "application/vnd.ms-excel", "list.xlsx") == "csv", "a CSV named .xlsx is a CSV")
    check(sniff(b"\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0" + b"\0" * 20, "application/vnd.ms-excel", "a.xls") == "legacy_office", "legacy .xls is recognised")

    # ---- hidden sheets ---------------------------------------------------------#
    e005 = ingest(DEV / "E005.eml")
    x = read_xlsx(e005.attachments[0].data, "Tank14.xlsx")
    check(x.meta["hidden_sheets_skipped"] == ["Rev A (old)"], "a hidden sheet is skipped")
    check("REV A" not in x.text.upper(), "and none of its rows reach the model")

    # ---- the cache contract ----------------------------------------------------#
    # These exact shapes are what the committed answers were recorded against.
    expected = {
        "E005": ("text", 16, 1),
        "E006": ("text", 57, 1),
        "E009": ("image", 0, 2),
        "E015": ("text", 19, 1),
        "E016": ("text", 7, 1),
        "E019": ("text", 17, 1),
        "E021": ("text", 55, 1),
        "E022": ("unreadable", 0, 0),
    }
    for eid, (kind, rows, n) in expected.items():
        e = ingest(DEV / f"{eid}.eml")
        doc = documentize(e.attachments[0])
        got_rows = len(doc.text.splitlines()) if doc.text else 0
        got_n = len(doc.images) if doc.kind == "image" else (1 if doc.kind == "text" else 0)
        check(
            doc.kind == kind and got_rows == rows and got_n == n,
            f"{eid} routes exactly as the cache was recorded",
            f"{doc.kind}/{got_rows} rows/{got_n}",
        )

    width = max(len(m) for _, m in checks) + 2
    for ok, msg in checks:
        print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {msg:<{width}}")
    failed = [m for ok, m in checks if not ok]
    print(f"\n{len(checks) - len(failed)}/{len(checks)} passed")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	# Running it
2	
3	## One setup step
4	
5	```bash
6	python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .
7	```
8	
9	Windows: `py -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\pip install -e .`
10	
11	Python 3.11+. Dependencies: `openai`, `openpyxl`, `python-docx`, `pymupdf`, `pillow` — all pure
12	wheels, no system packages, no poppler, no tesseract. Nothing is Linux-specific, so there is no
13	Dockerfile to need.
14	
15	## The command
16	
17	```bash
18	rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
19	```
20	
21	or, without installing:
22	
23	```bash
24	python parse.py parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
25	```
26	
27	`--out parsed.json` also writes `parsed.cost.json` beside it. Add `--traces traces/` for a
28	per-email record of what was found, what each document was judged to be, and every line that
29	was dropped and why.
30	
31	Exit codes: `0` the run completed; `2` it completed but some emails could not reach a model
32	(those come back flagged); `1` it could not start.
33	
34	## The API key
35	
36	Read from `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or from a `.env` file beside this README containing
37	`OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...`. 
38	
39	**With no key at all the dev inbox still runs**, replayed from the recorded answers in
40	`cache/`, and produces byte-identical output. That is the property the brief asks for, and it
41	is tested below.
42	
43	## Models
44	
45	| stage | default | why |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| classify | `gpt-4.1-mini` | short input, one cheap call, gates everything downstream |
48	| extract (text) | `gpt-4.1` | the context-carrying judgement lives here |
49	| extract (pictures) | `gpt-4.1` | photos, scans, pasted screenshots |
50	
51	Override per run with `--model-classify / --model-extract / --model-vision`, or the env vars
52	`RFQ_MODEL_CLASSIFY / RFQ_MODEL_EXTRACT / RFQ_MODEL_VISION`.
53	
54	These are the models the committed cache was recorded with, so a keyless replay only works on
55	the defaults. If your key cannot reach one of them, `rfq/llm.py` falls through to the nearest
56	equivalent (`gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`) rather than failing the email, and records the answer
57	under the model that was *asked for* so later replays still hit.
58	
59	The account this was built with also reached `gpt-5.x`. I did not default to it: it is not
60	universally available on other keys, I cannot report its price accurately, and on the one
61	measurement that mattered it was not better — see `DECISIONS.md`.
62	
63	## What a run costs
64	
65	Dev inbox, 24 emails, from an empty cache:
66	
67	```
68	58 model calls · 96,424 prompt tokens · 19,891 completion tokens · $0.2882
69	$0.0120 per email
70	```
71	
72	Spread is wide and deliberate. The four emails that carry no items — a vendor quote, a status
73	inquiry, a bounce, a newsletter — cost **$0.0007 each**, because classification runs first and
74	stops there. The expensive ones are the big documents: `$0.0380` for the 32-line two-page phone
75	scan, `$0.0332` for the 44-line PDF, `$0.0317` for the 50-line two-tab workbook.
76	
77	A second run on the same inbox costs **$0.0000** and makes **0** model calls.
78	
79	`parsed.cost.json` always reports both what this run spent and what the inbox would cost cold,
80	so a replay still tells you the real number. Prices come from the table in `rfq/llm.py` and are
81	printed with the report; override with `RFQ_PRICE_<MODEL>_IN` / `_OUT` if they drift.
82	
83	## Verifying the four properties
84	
85	```bash
86	# 1 + 2 — replayable with no key, and free the second time
87	rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out a.json      # cold: 58 calls, $0.2882
88	rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out b.json      # 0 calls, $0.0000
89	mv .env .env.off && rfq parse --emails data/dev/emails --out c.json && mv .env.off .env
90	shasum -a 256 a.json b.json c.json                   # all three identical
91	
92	# 3 — one bad email never takes down the run
93	python tests/test_resilience.py
94	
95	# the thread split, across 13 mail clients — free, no model, no key
96	python tests/test_quoted_split.py
97	
98	# how bytes become documents, incl. the shapes the cache was recorded against — free
99	python tests/test_documents.py
100	
101	# input shapes the dev inbox does not contain (needs a key; ~$0.09 cold)
102	python tests/test_shapes.py
103	
104	# 4 — cost
105	cat parsed.cost.json
106	```
107	
108	## Scoring it yourself
109	
110	```bash
111	python scripts/score.py parsed.json data/dev/answer_key.json
112	python scripts/score.py parsed.json data/dev/answer_key.json --detail E009
113	python data/check_format.py parsed.json --emails data/dev/emails
114	```
115	
116	`scripts/score.py` implements the brief's metrics in the order it says it grades them, with the
117	spelling-equivalence table the README describes. Current dev numbers are in `DECISIONS.md`.
118	
119	## Screen recording
120	
121	<!-- TODO: paste the link here before sending. -->
122	
123	## Layout
124	
125	```
126	rfq/ingest.py      MIME, body text, current-vs-quoted split, header signals, fingerprints
127	rfq/documents.py   attachments -> uniform Documents; routing by magic bytes
128	rfq/classify.py    the seven classes, the code vetoes, the cost gate
129	rfq/extract.py     per-document extraction, page strips, revision merge
130	rfq/verify.py      groundedness, uom vocabulary, qty sanity, de-duplication
131	rfq/link.py        duplicates, revisions, the needs_review rules
132	rfq/llm.py         the single model call site: cache, cost ledger, retries, fallbacks
133	rfq/prompts.py     what the model is told
134	rfq/pipeline.py    phase A (parallel, per email) and phase B (ordered, per inbox)
135	cache/             recorded model answers — committed, this is what makes replay work
136	scripts/score.py   the grader, as described in data/README.md
137	tests/             the resilience inbox
138	```

## Stack — stdlib Python + one HTML file

| option | verdict |
|---|---|
| Static HTML over `parsed.json` | ✗ can't accept dropped files — no pipeline |
| **stdlib `http.server` + vanilla JS** | ✓ **recommend** |
| FastAPI + React | ✗ adds deps + a build step; breaks "one setup step" |

No new dependencies, no build, works on Windows, and `pip install -e .` stays the only setup step. Polish is worth nothing.

That worked, and it immediately surfaced three things worth fixing. Look at the real output:

```
bayoucontracting.example
  └─ [REVISED ] pricing - bayou chemical tie-in     → 8 items (from E004)
       E003  10-06 08:47  rfq            8 items

hollismech.example                    ← not ridgeline-supply: the rep-forward
  └─ [NEW     ] condensate return material list     → 6 items (from E016)
```

24 emails collapse to **22 requests across 22 parties**, and the thread logic the brief tests becomes the navigation.

## Three problems it exposed

| what happened | why it's wrong | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `sabinevalve.example` listed as a customer with an open request | it's a **supplier** quoting *us* (E011) | derive a **party type** from classification |
| `gulfpipeflange.example` shows status `NEW` | it's a marketing blast (E014) — not a request at all | third bucket: *no action* |
| `mx1.ridgeline-supply.example` appears as a customer | it's our own mail server bouncing (E013) | same bucket; attribute to the supplier we failed to reach |

So the rollup needs three buckets, not one list:

```
CUSTOMERS   → open requests        (rfq · rfq_revision · purchase_order)
SUPPLIERS   → quotes we received   (vendor_quote)
NO ACTION   → bounces, newsletters (auto_reply · other)
```

## The data model

```
Party        domain, display name, type: customer | supplier | none
  └─ Request thread key, customer ref (PF-26-3091), status, current order
        └─ Email  E003 … E004 (revision) … E008 (duplicate)
              └─ Line items, each with source + provenance
```

**Status**, all derivable from what we already emit:

`NEW` · `REVISED` (a revision in the thread) · `ORDERED` (a PO) · `CHASED` (a status inquiry) · `NEEDS REVIEW`

**Current order** = the latest non-duplicate email in the thread that carries items. For Bayou that's E004's 8 lines, not E003's. That's the single most useful thing on the screen — *what do I quote right now.*

And because we have both, the UI can show **what changed**:

```
E004 changed the request:
  line 2   10 → 14 jts
  line 6   removed  (2" malleable union)
  line 9   added    (4 ea 2" bronze ball valve, 125#)
```

That's the revision logic made visible — one of the two decisions I'd put in front of them.

## The constraint I'd hold firmly

**`parsed.json` does not change.** The graded contract is one object per `.eml`, keyed by filename stem, and they run it before reading a word we wrote. The rollup is a *derived view*:

```
rfq/rollup.py   parsed.json + traces/  →  requests.json
```

Separate module, separate artifact, zero risk to the deliverable. The UI reads `requests.json` for navigation and `traces/<id>.json` for the per-email walkthrough.

## Build order

1. `rfq/rollup.py` + `rfq parse --requests requests.json` — ~120 lines, no model calls, testable immediately
2. `ui/server.py` — drop files, run, serve
3. `ui/index.html` — three-pane: parties → requests → the email walkthrough we designed
4. Accept / overturn → `ui/decisions.jsonl`

One honest note on scope: your core deliverable is finished and verified, and both of these are explicitly unscored — *"never required, never penalised when skipped… weighed in the interview, not in your score."* So this is worth building because it makes the demo much stronger, not because it adds points. If time gets tight, **step 1 alone** is worth it — it's cheap and it's the thing that proves you understood that a request is a thread, not an email.

which rows are items, and which context belongs on which line. Those are reading judgements and
no amount of regex does them.

Between the two sits the thing I'd defend first: **every extracted line's `raw` must actually
occur in the document it claims to come from**, by token coverage rather than substring (a
pasted spreadsheet splits one row across three lines, so substring is too strict). Lines that
fail are dropped. This is not theoretical — on E006 the call reading the 44-line PDF tried to
emit the two gasket lines that live in the email body, because the body is supplied as ambient
context. Code dropped them before they shipped. Precision is a property of the system, not a
hope about a prompt.

The second thing I'd defend: **quoted history is excluded from what the model sees**, not
merely labelled. E012 is a status inquiry with an entire seven-line RFQ pasted underneath;
nothing about it reaches the extractor, so there is no opportunity to hallucinate it, and the
groundedness check would drop it even if there were.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The deterministic layer: how bytes become documents.  No model, no key, free.

Everything here was a defect at some point, so everything here is a regression
test. The two at the top were found by building an input shape the dev inbox does
not contain, verified by hand, and then had no test guarding them — which is a fix
waiting to come undone.

The dev-routing block at the end exists for a different reason: it pins the exact
text the committed cache was recorded against. Change how a PDF or a sheet is
rendered and every recorded answer silently stops matching, the keyless replay
breaks, and the run looks fine while calling the model for all 24 emails.

    python tests/test_documents.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from rfq.documents import (  # noqa: E402
    MAX_DOC_ROWS,
    cap_rows,
    documentize,
    documentize_all,
    read_pdf,
    read_xlsx,
    sniff,
)
from rfq.extract import CHUNK_ROWS, _chunks  # noqa: E402
from rfq.ingest import ingest  # noqa: E402

DEV = REPO / "data" / "dev" / "emails"
checks: list[tuple[bool, str]] = []


def check(ok: bool, label: str, detail: str = "") -> None:
    checks.append((bool(ok), f"{label}{('  — ' + detail) if detail else ''}"))


def _sheet(n_rows: int) -> bytes:
    from openpyxl import Workbook

    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "FITTINGS - SW 3000#"
    ws.append(["Unit 9 - full BOM"])
    ws.append(["ALL FITTINGS SW 3000# A105 UNLESS NOTED"])
    ws.append(["ITEM", "QTY", "UOM", "SIZE", "DESCRIPTION"])
    for i in range(1, n_rows + 1):
        ws.append([i, (i % 40) + 1, "EA", '1-1/2"', "90 Elbow"])
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def _hybrid_pdf() -> bytes:
    """A typed covering note with a screenshot of a BOM pasted into it."""
    import pymupdf

    shot = ingest(DEV / "E010.eml").attachments[0].data  # a real spreadsheet screenshot
    doc = pymupdf.open()
    page = doc.new_page()
    page.insert_text((60, 70), "Ridgeline RFQ - Job 4412 shutdown materials", fontsize=13)
    page.insert_text((60, 95), "Please quote the items on the sheet below.", fontsize=10)
    page.insert_image(pymupdf.Rect(60, 120, 520, 460), stream=shot)
    page.insert_text((60, 500), "Delivery to Plant 2 dock. Terms net 30.", fontsize=10)
    return doc.tobytes()


class _Att:
    def __init__(self, filename, mime, data):
        self.filename, self.mime, self.data = filename, mime, data
        self.inline, self.content_id, self.size = False, None, len(data)


def main() -> int:
    # ---- a PDF carrying BOTH text and pictures -------------------------------- #
    # Was: any text layer meant "text document" and the pixels were never read, so a
    # screenshot of the order was invisible.  Silent, because the covering note parses.
    d = read_pdf(_hybrid_pdf(), "hybrid.pdf")
    check(d.kind == "mixed", "hybrid PDF is routed as mixed", f"got {d.kind!r}")
    check(len(d.images) >= 1, "its embedded picture is extracted", f"{len(d.images)} image(s)")
    check("Job 4412" in d.text, "its typed text is still read")

    # a logo-sized raster must NOT drag a page into mixed
    import pymupdf

    small = pymupdf.open()
    p = small.new_page()
    p.insert_text((60, 70), "Please quote the list below: 10 ea 2in gate valve, 800#", fontsize=11)
    p.insert_image(pymupdf.Rect(40, 700, 110, 740), stream=ingest(DEV / "E017.eml").attachments[0].data)
    d2 = read_pdf(small.tobytes(), "letterhead.pdf")
    check(d2.kind == "text", "a letterhead logo does not make a page mixed", f"got {d2.kind!r}")

    # ---- a spreadsheet past the row cap --------------------------------------- #
    # Was: truncated at 60k characters inside the extractor with truncated=False,

## Optional: the viewer

```bash
rfq-ui                 # or: python ui/server.py
```

Opens `http://127.0.0.1:8765` (loopback only — nothing here talks to anything but the model
provider). Drop `.eml` files on the page. They run through the same pipeline `rfq parse` uses
and replay from the committed cache, so the dev inbox returns in under a second for $0.00.

It is a viewer, not a second implementation. Everything on screen comes from `parse`'s own
output and per-email traces. It never writes `parsed.json`, `cache/` or anything else the
submission depends on; the only file it creates is `ui/decisions.jsonl`.

**What it shows.** The left pane groups the inbox the way a rep works — parties, then requests,
then the messages in each. A request is a thread, not an email: E003 and E004 are one request
whose order changed, E006 and E008 are one request sent twice. Suppliers and no-action mail
(bounces, marketing) are bucketed separately so they never sit in the queue looking live.

Clicking a message walks it through the six stages:

1. **the message** — with the thread history greyed out and labelled *not given to the
   extractor*. On E012 you can see a whole seven-line RFQ sitting in that grey zone.

3. **classification** — the label, the model's reason, and any code override
4. **line items kept** — click a line for its `raw` and the headings its context came from
5. **dropped by verification** — what was thrown away and why
6. **outcome** — the review flag and what that email cost

real mail, that file is the only labelled data that exists — see the end of `DECISIONS.md`.

python ui/rollup.py parsed.json --emails data/dev/emails   # the grouping, on the console
```

Noted on the UI — we'll redo it when you come back.

Here's the flow, step by step, with **E006** as the running example and every AI call marked.

---

## E006 arrives

```
From:    Marguerite Dubois <mdubois@pelicanfab.example>
Subject: RFQ PF-26-3091 flanges
Body:    "Hi team, RFQ attached, need it back by Friday.
          Also please add:
          - 2 sets of 4" 150# spiral wound gaskets, 304 SS/graphite
          - 6 sets of 6" 150# spiral wound gaskets, 304 SS/graphite"
Attached: RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf
```

---

## STEP 1 — Open the envelope   `CODE ONLY · no AI`

**IN:** the raw `.eml` file (bytes)

**What happens:** unpack the email. Pull out sender, subject, date, body text, attachments. Then **split the body in two** — what they wrote *now* vs the old thread quoted below.

**OUT:**
```
from:        mdubois@pelicanfab.example
subject:     RFQ PF-26-3091 flanges
body_now:    "Hi team, RFQ attached... Also please add: 2 sets..."
body_quoted: ""                    ← E006 has no thread
attachments: [RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf]
```

> Why the split matters: in **E012** `body_now` is 144 characters ("any update?") and `body_quoted` is 583 characters containing a whole 7-line RFQ. The quoted half never goes to the AI. That one decision prevents most hallucinated lines.

**AI calls so far: 0**

---

## STEP 2 — Turn attachments into documents   `CODE ONLY · no AI`

**IN:** `RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf` (4,927 bytes)

**What happens:** look at the *bytes* (not the filename) to decide what it is → it's a PDF → does it have real text inside, or is it a scan? This one has text. Rebuild the table columns from the word positions.

**OUT:** a **document** — a name plus text:
```
source: "RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf"
kind:   text
text:   RFQ No.: | PF-26-3091 | Required By: | 10/22/2026
        Material: | ASTM A105
        Rating: | 150# RF
        ITEM | QTY | UOM | SIZE | DESCRIPTION
        1 | 7 | EA | 1/2" | WELD NECK FLANGE, STD BORE
        2 | 3 | EA | 3/4" | WELD NECK FLANGE, STD BORE
        ... 40 more rows
```

Every format ends up as the same thing — a **name + text**, or a **name + pictures**:

| arrives | becomes |
|---|---|
| Excel | text (hidden sheets skipped, tab name on top) |
| Word / CSV | text |
| PDF **with** text | text |
| PDF **without** text (a scan) | pictures |
| photo / screenshot | pictures |
| encrypted / corrupt | "can't read" |

**AI calls so far: 0**

---

## STEP 3 — What kind of email is this?   ⚡ **AI CALL #1**

**IN:** headers + `body_now` + a short preview of each document

**The AI is asked:** *"Which of these 7 is this message doing?"* — rfq, rfq_revision, purchase_order, vendor_quote, status_inquiry, auto_reply, other.

**Model:** `gpt-4.1-mini` (the cheap one — short input, simple question)

**It returns:**
```json
{ "classification": "rfq",
  "why": "asks us to price the attached flange schedule plus two gasket lines" }
```

**Then CODE can overrule it.** If the headers say bounce, it's `auto_reply` no matter what the AI said — that's how E013's bounce (which contains a complete 4-item order) never becomes a request.

### 🔑 This step is a gate

```
rfq · rfq_revision · purchase_order   →  carry on to step 4
everything else                       →  STOP. Output empty list.
```

**That's why E011, E012, E013, E014 cost $0.0007 each** — one cheap call and done. They never reach the expensive step.

**AI calls so far: 1**

---

## STEP 4 — Read each document   ⚡ **AI CALL #2 and #3**

This is the expensive step. **One AI call per document.** E006 has two documents, so two calls.

### Call #2 — the body

**IN:** the body text, plus a note listing the attachments as background

**The AI is asked:** *"What line items are in THIS text? Write each one self-contained."*

**Model:** `gpt-4.1` (the strong one — this is where the judgement is)

**It returns:**
```json
[{ "raw": "2 sets of 4\" 150# spiral wound gaskets, 304 SS/graphite",
   "description": "4\" 150# spiral wound gasket, 304 SS/graphite",
   "qty": 2, "uom": "SET" },
 { ... 6" gasket ... }]
```

### Call #3 — the PDF

**IN:** the PDF's text, plus the email subject and body as background

**The AI is asked:** the same question, about this document.

**It returns 42 lines**, each one carrying context from elsewhere on the page:
```json
{ "raw": "1 | 7 | EA | 1/2\" | WELD NECK FLANGE, STD BORE",
  "description": "1/2\" weld neck flange, 150# RF, A105, STD bore",
  "qty": 7, "uom": "EA",
  "context_from": ["form field: Material: ASTM A105",
                   "form field: Rating: 150# RF"] }
```

> **Notice what it did.** The row says only `1/2" WELD NECK FLANGE`. The words *A105* and *150# RF* are form fields at the **top of the page**. Carrying them down onto every row — and onto the *right* rows — is the main thing being graded.

**Why one call per document and not one per email?**

- `source` is correct automatically (the document knows its own name)
- a 300-page PDF can't blow up one prompt
- documents can be read in parallel
- a broken document takes down only itself

**AI calls so far: 3**

---

## STEP 5 — Check what the AI said   `CODE ONLY · no AI`

**IN:** 44 suggested lines + the text of the document each one claims to come from

**What happens:** the AI's answer is treated as **evidence, not truth**. Code checks every line:

| check | throws away |
|---|---|
| are these words actually in that document? | lines copied from somewhere else |
| is this row a heading / total / price label? | `TOTAL QTY \| 35` |
| is the unit one of the 14 allowed? | anything else → `null` |
| did they state a number at all? | `"a couple caps"` → `null` |

> **This caught a real error during development.** While reading the PDF, the AI also returned the two *gasket* lines — because it could see the body as background. Code asked *"are those words in the PDF?"* → no → **dropped**. (I later fixed the prompt so it stops doing that, so this no longer triggers on dev. It's covered by a unit test instead.)

**OUT:** 44 verified lines

**AI calls so far: 3**

---

## STEP 6 — Look at the whole inbox   `CODE ONLY · no AI`

This step needs the *other* emails, so it runs last, in date order.

**What happens:**
- **Duplicate?** E008 has the same sender, same subject (minus `RESEND:`), and a **byte-identical PDF** → `duplicate_of: E006`, zero lines
- **Revision?** E004 replies to E003 changing it → merge into the complete order
- **Can't read something?** → `needs_review` + reason

**OUT for E006:**
```json
{ "classification": "rfq",
  "revises": null,
  "duplicate_of": null,
  "needs_review": false,
  "line_items": [ ...44 lines... ] }
```

---

## One exception: a revision needs an extra AI call

When step 3 says `rfq_revision` (like E004), there's **⚡ one more AI call in step 6**:

**IN:** E003's 8 recorded lines + E004's text *("line 2 is now 14 jts, drop the unions, add ball valves")*

**The AI is asked:** *"Apply these changes. Give me the complete order as it now stands."*

**OUT:** 8 lines — qty changed, union gone, ball valve added.

---

## The whole picture

| step | AI? | model | what it decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Open envelope | **no** | — | current vs quoted |
| 2 Documents | **no** | — | what each file is |
| 3 Classify | ⚡ **yes** | `4.1-mini` | which of 7 kinds |
| 4 Read documents | ⚡ **yes ×N** | `4.1` | which rows are items, what context they carry |
| 5 Verify | **no** | — | what actually ships |
| 6 Link & flag | **no** | — | duplicates, revisions, review |

**AI calls per email = 1 + (number of documents), and 1 if it's not a request at all.**

Real numbers from the dev run:

```
E011 vendor quote    1 call    $0.0007   ← stopped at step 3
E014 newsletter      1 call    $0.0007   ← stopped at step 3
E006 body + PDF      3 calls   $0.0332
E009 body + 2 pages  4 calls   $0.0380
───────────────────────────────────────
24 emails           58 calls   $0.2882   ($0.012 each)
second run           0 calls   $0.0000   ← everything cached
```

## The one sentence that explains all of it

> **The AI only ever reads. Code decides what ships.**

The AI is good at *"which words on this page belong to this line"* — no regex does that. It is not trusted with *"does this line exist"*, *"is EA a valid unit"*, *"is this a duplicate"*, or *"should a human look at this"*. Those are all code, because they can be checked.

"""Drives the pipeline one email at a time so the viewer can show it happening.

This is not a second implementation. It calls the same `process_email`, the same
`link_inbox`, the same `resolve_revisions` that `rfq parse` calls, in the same
order. What it adds is bookkeeping: which step each email is on, and — through
the ModelRunner's observer — exactly what was sent to the model and what came
back, so the page can put the prompt next to the email next to the result.

Sequential on purpose. `rfq parse` runs six emails at once because it is trying
to finish; this is trying to be watched.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
import threading
import time
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from rfq.cli import _load_dotenv, default_cache  # noqa: E402
from rfq.ingest import ingest  # noqa: E402
from rfq.link import ITEM_CLASSES, apply_needs_review, link_inbox  # noqa: E402
from rfq.llm import ModelRunner  # noqa: E402
from rfq.pipeline import (  # noqa: E402
    DEFAULT_CLASSIFY_MODEL,
    DEFAULT_EXTRACT_MODEL,
    DEFAULT_VISION_MODEL,
    process_email,
    resolve_revisions,
)

STEPS = [
    ("ingest", "Open the envelope", "split the current message from the thread below it"),
    ("documents", "Read the attachments", "every file becomes text or pictures"),
    ("classify", "What kind of email?", "one of seven — and a gate: four of them stop here"),
    ("extract", "Read each document", "one model call per document"),
    ("verify", "Check every line", "does it really occur in the document it claims?"),
    ("link", "Place it in the inbox", "duplicate? revision? does a human need to look?"),
]

_DOC = re.compile(r"=== THE (DOCUMENT|PICTURE): (.+?) ===")


def _label(rec: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """A human name for a model call, and which document it was about."""
    schema, user = rec.get("schema", ""), "\n".join(rec.get("user") or [])
    if schema.startswith("email_classification"):
        second = "second_look" in schema
        return ("Decide what this email is" + (" (second look)" if second else ""), "")
    if schema == "revised_order":
        return ("Apply the customer's changes to the earlier order", "body")
    m = _DOC.search(user)
    where = m.group(2) if m else "body"
    kind = "picture" if (m and m.group(1) == "PICTURE") else "document"
    return (f"Read the {kind}: {where}", where)


class Job:
    """All the state the page polls for."""

    def __init__(self, job_id: str, inbox: Path, queue: list[dict]) -> None:
        self.id = job_id
        self.inbox = inbox
        self.state = "staged"
        self.started: float | None = None
        self.elapsed = 0.0
        self.error: str | None = None
        self.order = [q["id"] for q in queue]
        self.queue = {q["id"]: q for q in queue}
        self.emails: dict[str, dict] = {
            q["id"]: {
                "id": q["id"],
                "state": "pending",
                "steps": {name: "pending" for name, _, _ in STEPS},
                "calls": [],
                "result": None,
                "summary": None,
                "error": None,
            }
            for q in queue
        }
        self.cost: dict | None = None
        self.results: list = []
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
        with self.lock:
            return {
                "job": self.id,
                "state": self.state,
                "error": self.error,
                "elapsed": round((time.time() - self.started) if self.started else 0.0, 1),
                "order": self.order,
                "queue": [self.queue[i] for i in self.order],

content.text:
Rebuilt and running at **http://127.0.0.1:8765** — it's open in your browser.

## How it works now

**1. Drop → stage.** Drag `data/dev/emails/` onto the page. Nothing runs. It reads the headers only and fills the queue — sender, subject, attachment count. Drop more whenever you like, they join the queue.

**2. Press Process.** Emails run **one at a time, in order**, so you can watch it. (`rfq parse` runs six at once because it's trying to finish; this is trying to be watched.) The queue dot pulses on the email being read.

**3. Each email shows the six steps as a rail:**

```
STEP 1 code     STEP 2 code      STEP 3 AI        STEP 4 AI        STEP 5 code    STEP 6 code
Open the        Read the         What kind of     Read each        Check every    Place it in
envelope        attachments      email?           document         line           the inbox
```

Green = done, blue = running, faded = **skipped**.

**4. Side by side, at the top:** the email exactly as it arrived (with the thread history greyed out underneath, labelled *never shown to the model*) next to the line items that came out of it.

**5. Then every model call, in full:**

```
┌ MODEL │ Read the document: RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf │ gpt-4.1 │ replayed from cache │ $0.0191 ┐
├─────────────────── what we sent ──────────┬────────── what came back ─────────────────┤
│ ▸ system prompt — the rules it was given  │  44 lines  item_list                      │
│ ▾ user message — what it was asked about  │  qty  uom  description                    │
│   === EMAIL CONTEXT ===                   │    7  EA   1/2" weld neck flange, 150#…   │
│   Subject: RFQ PF-26-3091 flanges         │    3  EA   3/4" weld neck flange, 150#…   │
│   === THE DOCUMENT: RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf === │  ▸ the raw JSON it returned               │
│   ITEM | QTY | UOM | SIZE | DESCRIPTION   │                                           │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Images sent to the model are rendered inline — on **E009** you'll see the actual scan strips that were sent for page 1 and page 2.

## Three to click

- **E011** — vendor quote. Step 4 reads **skipped**. One call, $0.0007. That's the cost gate made visible.
- **E012** — status inquiry. The greyed block under the body is a whole 7-line RFQ the model never saw.
- **E009** — the scan. Four calls: classify, body, then *"Read the picture: page 1 of 2"* and *page 2 of 2*, with the strip images shown.

## One thing I noticed while testing

Production splits E009's pages into **2 strips**, not 3 — `round(1728 / 700) = 2`. My original experiment that got 28/28 used 3. The 2 remaining qty errors on dev are on that page, so dropping the strip target to ~600px would likely fix them. It's a 1-line change on `master`, but it invalidates the image cache and needs a paid re-run, so I've left it as a lead rather than doing it unasked.

6	the ModelRunner's observer — exactly what was sent to the model and what came
7	back, so the page can put the prompt next to the email next to the result.
8	
9	Sequential on purpose. `rfq parse` runs six emails at once because it is trying

Each cell carries its state on the left border — green done, blue running, amber warning. A column of green with one amber cell reads as an inbox at a glance.

Blue = code decides, purple = a model reads. The gate drops off step 3 with the cost consequence written next to it. `hide` collapses it once you've seen it.

```
Bayoucontracting   bayoucontracting.example   Terrence Bailey    1 request · 2 messages · 8 lines to quote
   Pricing - Bayou Chemical tie-in     749ch   no thread   0 files   rfq            1 call    8 kept   ready
   E003 · Oct 6

   revision     E004 · Oct 6

Pelicanfab         pelicanfab.example         Marguerite Dubois  1 request · 2 messages · 44 lines to quote
   RFQ PF-26-3091 flanges              228ch   no thread   1 file    rfq            2 calls  44 kept   ready
   E006 · Oct 8
 ↳ RESEND: RFQ PF-26-3091 flanges      268ch   no thread   1 file    rfq            2 calls   0 kept   duplicate
   duplicate    E008 · Oct 9                                                                           superseded by E006
```

Each party gets a heading with **how many lines are actually waiting to be quoted** — that's the number counted from whichever message spoke last, so Bayou shows **8** (E004's revised order), not 16.

Three things the grouping makes visible:

- **`current order`** in the outcome column marks which message in a thread to work from. E004 has it; E003 just says `ready`.
- **`superseded by E006`** on the duplicate, so nobody quotes it twice.
- **A separate request from the same party stays on its own top-level line** — only revisions and duplicates indent.

Two label fixes while I was there:

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| E016 (rep forward) | `Ridgeline Supply` | **`Hollismech`** — files under the customer, not the colleague who forwarded it |
| E013 (bounce) | `Mx1` | **`Ridgeline (us)`** — our own mail server never reads like a customer with an open request |

One design note worth knowing: threading uses the pipeline's real `revises`/`duplicate_of` links once an email has been read. *Before* it's read, the normalised subject is the only hint, so that's used provisionally — but it's deliberately **not** reapplied afterwards. Two different orders can share a generic subject like "pricing request", and the duplicate rule has already decided they aren't the same request; re-merging on subject would undo that.

1	"""A local viewer for the RFQ pipeline: drop .eml files, press Process, watch it work.
2	
3	Stdlib only, no build step, no new dependencies.  Imports rfq as a library and
4	writes nothing the graded submission depends on.
5	
6	    rfq-ui                 # or: python ui/server.py
7	    → http://127.0.0.1:8765
8	
9	Binds to loopback only.  The brief forbids outbound side effects beyond the model
10	provider, and nothing here talks to anything else.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import base64
16	import json
17	import mimetypes
18	import shutil
19	import sys
20	import tempfile
21	import threading
22	import time

26	from pathlib import Path

30	REPO = HERE.parent
31	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

34	from rfq.ingest import ingest, ingest_bytes  # noqa: E402
35	from ui import engine, rollup  # noqa: E402

37	JOBS: dict[str, engine.Job] = {}

44	
45	def stage_files(files: list[dict], job_id: str | None = None) -> engine.Job:
46	    """Save uploads and read their headers.  No model call, nothing spent."""
47	    job = JOBS.get(job_id or "")
48	    if job is None or job.state == "running":
49	        work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rfq-ui-"))
50	        inbox = work / "emails"
51	        inbox.mkdir(parents=True)
52	        job_id = f"job-{int(time.time() * 1000)}"
53	    else:
54	        inbox = job.inbox
55	
56	    for f in files:
57	        name = Path(f.get("name", "mail.eml")).name
58	        if not name.lower().endswith(".eml"):
59	            name += ".eml"
60	        target = inbox / name
61	        n = 1
62	        while target.exists():

Refresh. Two changes:

## 1. Attachments are real files now

Each document in the **Attachments** panel has its size and a **download** link that serves the actual bytes with the right content type:

```
RFQ_PF-26-3091.pdf     text  item_list  4.8 KB  [download]
Scan_RFQ_SC-4418.pdf   image  item_list  182 KB  [download]
SR-4-117_Unit4_BOM.xlsx  text  item_list  6.7 KB  [download]
```

It walks **into forwarded messages** too — so a spreadsheet hanging off an inner `.eml` downloads under its own name. That's the case where the order most often actually lives.

## 2. The grid breathes

The problem in your screenshot was that **every cell** had a coloured left stripe. A perfectly healthy inbox rendered as a wall of green bars, so nothing stood out and the eye had nowhere to rest.

Now:

- **Each email is a bordered card** with rounded corners and real spacing between them
- A cell is simply **dimmed** until its stage has run, **faded** when the stage was skipped — no colour
- State lives **once, on the card's border**: blue while running, amber for needs-review, red for failed
- A revision or duplicate **hangs off its parent on a drawn connector** instead of just being indented
- The `view ›` affordance moved to the cell's bottom-right corner and only appears on hover

So the eye now goes: party heading → cards → the one amber card. E017 and E022 should be the only things that pull attention on the dev inbox.

Two spots to check: **Bayou** (E004 connected under E003, outcome `current order`) and **Pelicanfab** (E008 connected under E006, outcome `superseded by E006`).

What's next — colours, column widths, or something in the panels?

content.text:
Clear answer: **right now, cache — zero real calls.** Here's the proof, both ways:

## What you're seeing on the dev inbox

```
0 calls · 58 cached · $0.0000 spent this run
```

Every one of those 58 answers **was** a real OpenAI call — I made them while building this. The cache directory holds **127 recorded answers**, recorded between 07:46 and 09:06 UTC today, which cost **$0.64 of real money**. They're committed to the repo.

That's the whole point of requirement #1 in the brief: *"On the dev inbox it runs with no API key — record or cache model responses and commit them."* The graders run your submission twice, the second time with the key removed, and both runs must match.

## Proof it still calls for real

I just fed it an email the cache has never seen:

```
=== a brand-new email ===
run: 2 real calls · 0 cached · $0.0045 actually spent

   CALLED OPENAI    gpt-4.1-mini   1182 in /  75 out  $0.0006  Decide what this email is
   CALLED OPENAI    gpt-4.1        1463 in / 122 out  $0.0039  Read the document: body
   lines extracted: 2

=== the same email again ===
run: 0 real calls · 2 cached · $0.0000 actually spent
```

First time: real money. Second time: free.

## How to tell in the UI

Every model call card carries the label:

| badge | meaning |
|---|---|
| **`called`** | went to OpenAI, cost real money, tokens are what it actually used |
| **`replayed from cache`** (green) | read from disk, $0.00, same answer as when it was recorded |

And the header meter splits it: `0 calls · 58 cached · $0.2882 cold`. The last figure is what the inbox *would* cost from an empty cache — so a replay still tells you the real number instead of reporting a misleading $0.00.

## What makes a cache hit

The key is a hash of **model + prompt version + the exact rendered prompt + image bytes**. So:

- same email, same prompts → **hit**
- one character changed in the email → **miss**, real call
- I edit a prompt in `rfq/prompts.py` → **every** answer that used it misses

That last one is why re-running after a prompt change costs the full $0.29 again — which is correct, because the old answers are no longer answers to the question being asked.

content.text:
Added — refresh the page. There's a **`live calls`** switch in the header, next to `add .eml`.

## What it does

```
OFF (default)   use the recorded answers        0 calls · $0.0000
ON              ignore them, call OpenAI        every call is real money
```

Flip it on and:
- a warning bar appears: *"every recorded answer is ignored — 24 emails will be sent to OpenAI for real, roughly $0.29"*
- the **Process** button turns amber and reads **"Run 24 live"**
- every call card says **`called`** instead of **`replayed from cache`**

Verified on the same email three times:

```
toggle OFF → 0 real · 2 cached · $0.0000 · ['cache', 'cache'] · 5 lines
toggle ON  → 2 real · 0 cached · $0.0058 · ['live',  'live' ] · 5 lines
toggle OFF → 0 real · 2 cached · $0.0000 · ['cache', 'cache'] · 5 lines
```

## Two deliberate constraints

**It doesn't write to the cache.** A live run leaves `cache/` byte-identical — verified, 127 files before and after. That matters because those committed answers are what make the keyless replay reproduce the graded run; a testing toggle must not be able to quietly rewrite them underneath that. So you can experiment freely without touching the submission.

*(New emails the cache has never seen still get recorded normally when the toggle is off — that's how you'd add to it deliberately.)*

**It warns before it spends.** The cost estimate comes from the cold figure the ledger already tracks, not a guess.

## One bug fixed along the way

Re-runs were **appending** to the call list, so a live run showed last run's cached calls *beside* this run's real ones — and neither count meant anything. A run now starts clean.

---

Worth knowing for your testing: the most interesting use is **changing a prompt in `rfq/prompts.py`, then running live on one email** to see whether the answer moves. Editing a prompt also invalidates its cache entries by design, so you'd get fresh answers on the next normal run anyway — the toggle just lets you check without committing to that.
